sentences.text: The petitioners are accused Nos.1, 2 and 3 - husband, Mother-in-law and Father-in-law of the 2nd respondent/complainant.

During the pendency of the proceedings before the concerned Court, the parties to the lis i.e., accused and the complainant have settled the matter amicably and have filed an application seeking compounding of the offences.

The joint affidavit filed in support of the compounding application reads as follows:
"We,
1) Manjunath A. A, S/o Ashok Alagarahuth, Aged about 40 years, the petitioner No.1;
2) Savitri, W/o.

Ashok Alagarahuth, S/o. Late Ishwarappa, Aged about 64 years, the petitioner No.2; 3) Ashok Alagarahuth, S/o. Late Ishwarappa, Aged about 69 years,
the petitioner No.3; All are residing at: #15, 1st Main, 1st Cross, Priyadarshini Layout,
Moodalapalya Main Road, Bengaluru - 560072, AND 4) Jayashree B S, D/o Sadashiv,
Aged About 38 Years, the respondent No.2, Residing At: #932, 12th Cross, 35th Main, 1st Stage, J.P.Nagar, Bengaluru, do here by solemnly affirm and state an oath as follows:
NC: 2024:KHC:19392 1.
We the above-named Petitioners and Respondent No.2 respectively in the above captioned case and well acquainted with the facts of the case.
Hence, we are swearing to the contents of this affidavit.
2. We are the petitioners and respondent No.2 in the above case and well versed with the facts of the case.

The we have amicably settled the differences between us and hence not interested to prosecute the case and hence I, Jayashree, the Respondent No.2 is the complainant and the victim has no objection to quash the proceedings which are subject matter in the captioned petition.
3. We submit that, whatever we stated above are true and correct to the best of our knowledge and belief and we believe the same to be true and correct.
THEREFORE, we pray that this Hon'ble court be pleased to quash the proceedings which are subject matter in the captioned petition, in the interest of justice and equity."

In the light of the offence being the one punishable under Section 498A of the IPC inter alia and not being against the State or punishable with imprisonment for life, I deem it appropriate to accept the application seeking compounding of the offence and compound the offence as aforesaid.

3. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Criminal Petition is allowed.
